items.en: Affect is usually a verb (to influence); effect is usually a noun (a result).
items.ex: Rain can affect the harvest; the effect is lower prices.
items.tip: A for Action (affect), E for End result (effect).

items.en: Accept means to receive or agree; except means leaving out.
items.ex: I accept every suggestion except the last one.

items.en: Advice is a noun (a suggestion); advise is a verb (to suggest).
items.ex: I advise you to follow your teacher's advice.
items.tip: Ice is a thing (advice); is is an action (advise).

items.en: Complement means to complete or suit; compliment means praise.
items.ex: The colours complement each other, and guests paid her a compliment.
items.tip: ComplEment complEtes; complIment: I like it.

items.en: Principal means main or head of a school; principle means a rule or belief.
items.ex: Our principal never breaks a principle.
items.tip: The principAL is your pAL; a principLE is a ruLE.

items.en: Stationary means not moving; stationery means paper and pens.
items.ex: The van was stationary outside the stationery shop.

items.en: Lose means fail to keep; loose means not tight.
items.ex: If the screw is loose, you may lose it.
items.tip: Loose has an extra o, like extra room.

items.en: Emigrate means leave your country; immigrate means come into a new country.
items.bn: দেশ ছেড়ে যাওয়া বনাম অন্য দেশে বসবাসে আসা
items.hi: देश छोड़ना बनाम दूसरे देश में आकर बसना
items.ex: They emigrate from India and immigrate to Canada.

items.en: Eminent means famous and respected; imminent means about to happen.
items.ex: An eminent scientist warned that a storm was imminent.

items.en: Council is a group of people; counsel means advice or to advise.
items.ex: The council sought legal counsel.

items.en: Desert is a dry land (or to abandon); dessert is a sweet dish.
items.ex: In the desert we dreamt of a cold dessert.
items.tip: Dessert has two s's: you want seconds.

items.en: Ensure means make certain; insure means protect with insurance.
items.ex: Ensure you insure your new bike.

items.en: Precede means come before; proceed means go forward.
items.ex: A short prayer will precede the event; then we will proceed.

items.en: Elicit means draw out; illicit means illegal.
items.ex: The officer tried to elicit details about the illicit trade.

items.en: Discreet means careful and tactful; discrete means separate.
items.ex: Be discreet; the data falls into discrete groups.
items.tip: In discrete, the t separates the e's.

items.en: Canvas is strong cloth; canvass means ask for votes or opinions.
items.ex: Volunteers carried canvas bags to canvass for votes.
items.tip: Canvass has an extra s for 'seeking support'.

items.en: Allusion is an indirect reference; illusion is a false appearance.
items.ex: The poem's allusion to the epic created an illusion of age.

items.en: Adapt means adjust; adopt means take as one's own.
items.ex: Families who adopt a pet must adapt their routine.

items.en: Continual means repeated often; continuous means without a break.
items.ex: Continual phone calls and continuous noise ruined the day.

items.en: Disinterested means fair and unbiased; uninterested means not interested.
items.ex: A disinterested referee is needed, not an uninterested one.
items.tip: A disinterested judge can still be very interested.
